stemMd: A restaurant will replace a popular dish with a higher-margin dish. Management expects total profit to rise. Which issue is most important to investigate?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Whether the old dish appears first alphabetically.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Whether the chef prefers a particular apron.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Whether diners use the same entrance.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Whether the new dish has a shorter name.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Whether the new dish’s sales and effects on other purchases will offset any lost demand for the old dish.

explanationMd: A higher margin per sale does not ensure higher total profit if quantity or complementary purchases fall. Demand and cross-purchase effects test the missing link.

distractorRationale.b: Personal attire is irrelevant to demand and margin.
distractorRationale.c: Entrance use does not address the profit calculation.
distractorRationale.d: Name length does not determine total contribution.
distractorRationale.a: Alphabetic position does not settle customer substitution.
